chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is the matter with me that I ask you a question and you answer me with one answer, then someone other than me comes to you, and you answer him with a different answer about the same question?' So he said: 'We answer people according to increase and decrease (of their capacity).'

He said: I said: 'Then inform me about the companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) — did they narrate truthfully from Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) or did they lie?' He said: 'Rather, they were truthful.' I said: 'Then what is the matter with them that they differed?' So he said: 'Do you not know that a man would come to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and ask him a question, and he would answer him regarding it with an answer, then he would answer him after that with what abrogated that answer — and so the narrations abrogated one another?'

key_terms.اختلفوا: They differed — referring to apparent contradictions among the Prophet's companions in their narrations
key_terms.الزيادة والنقصان: Increase and decrease — referring to the varying spiritual capacity, readiness, and level of understanding of different questioners
key_terms.نسخ/نسخت: Abrogation — the Islamic legal and Quranic doctrine whereby a later ruling supersedes an earlier one; here applied to hadith narrations

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq give different answers to different people asking the same question?
ai.summary: This hadith records a dialogue between Mansur ibn Hazim, a companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), and the Imam himself. The narrator asks why the Imam gives different answers to different questioners asking the same question. The Imam explains that his answers vary according to the spiritual and intellectual capacity of each questioner — a pedagogical principle of tailored guidance. The narrator then asks about apparent contradictions among the companions of the Prophet, and the Imam explains this through the doctrine of abrogation (naskh): the Prophet himself sometimes gave different answers to the same question at different times, with later revelations or rulings superseding earlier ones, causing apparent contradictions among honest narrators who heard the Prophet at different times.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Mansour Bin Hazim who said, 
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is the matter that I ask you<sup>asws</sup> the question, so you<sup>asws</sup> answer me with regards to it with the answer, then there comes to you other than me, so you<sup>asws</sup> answer him with another answer, regarding his question?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> answer the people sometimes more and sometimes less (as per their merit/status)’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘So inform me about the companions of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. Were they truthful upon Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> or they lied (while reporting)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But they (generally) were truthful’. I said, ‘So what is the matter with them that they are differing?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you not know that the man would come to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and he would ask him<sup>saww</sup> the question, so he<sup>saww</sup> would answer him with regards to it with an answer. Then he<sup>saww</sup> would answer him after that what Abrogated that answer. So the Ahadeeth got Abrogated by the other (Ahadeeth)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Najran from ‘Asim ibn Humayd from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said the following. “I said to (Imam) abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.), ‘It is confuses me that when I ask you a question and you give an answer and then other person comes and you give a different answer for the same question.’” The Imam replied, “We answer people in a larger and reduced forms.”

I then asked, “Did the Sahabah, companions of the holy Prophet speak the truth or lies when narrating his Hadith?” The Imam replied, “They spoke the truth.” I then said, “Why then they have differences?” Have you not considered the fact that a man would come to the holy Prophet (s.a.) and ask a question and would give him an answer and then he would answer that would abrogate the previous answer. Thus, Ahadith abrogated other Ahadith.”
